deep.reconstruction:
This is a front flyleaf (pastedown) of a pocket notebook ('Gauß Varia 10', old shelfmark 21.1043). It holds unrelated memoranda, some written upside down. It contains no mathematical derivation.

(a) Top: an astronomical bibliographic note. 'Mädler. A.N. 192' (overwritten, possibly 162) cites an Astronomische Nachrichten number. '4½füss[ig] 43 Linien' describes the instrument: a refractor of 4½ (Paris) feet focal length and 43 lines aperture. This fits the Fraunhofer refractor Beer and Mädler used in Berlin. '10 Apr. 1. 4. 14,73' looks like a date with a time or reading. '2^Vol = 447' is probably a page reference.

(b) 1820, household record. The 3rd Klafter of firewood was received on 17 May, the 4th on 25 May, and the 5th on 26 May, 'und die Hälfte des Sechsten' (and half of the sixth). From the 3rd onward that is 3.5 Klafter (my inference), or 5.5 Klafter cumulatively.

(c) Coin measurement. '9 Doppelthaler = 369.5 mm Breite, = 29.1 Dicke'. Nine double thalers laid edge to edge span 369.5 mm, and stacked they are 29.1 mm thick. Per coin (my computation): diameter 369.5/9 = 41.06 mm and thickness 29.1/9 = 3.23 mm. Both agree well with the Vereinsdoppeltaler (from 1839), so this entry is late, at least 1839.

(d) 'Stärke 39 / 65 / A 670 / B 216' is an unexplained list. It may record thread strengths or weights, possibly silk suspension threads given the later 'Seid.' entries. This reading is speculative.

(e) Upside-down block: weights and coin data.
- 'Gewicht 37,77', 'Breite 5,314', '1/12 0,966' are weights or dimensions of coins, perhaps in grams or Loth.
- '1 Loth G = 0,9' and '1/12 … = 0,216'.
- '4¾ … 1/12 5x = 1 Dgr' is a conversion.
- 'Gr.BM 34 … C gr. seid. = 280', 'Gr.N {20, 19} = 375 gr', 'Seid 18 … 1 = 62.5' look like comparative weights or strengths of silk ('seid.') and other materials or items.
- 'leicht 58.6', 'Seidn. neu schw. 63.8', 'Gr.M. 64.87' are a further set of weights.

The next page holds the same kind of coin and weight tables (coins per Hanoverian pound, Hessian 1/6, Prussian Louis d'or, etc.). That makes it likely that (e) is part of Gauss's practical metrology of coin weights and thicknesses.

No mathematics beyond simple division is involved.
errors: No mathematical errors are identifiable. Several numerical entries (Stärke list, Seid/Gr.N/Gr.BM values) are too cryptic to check internally. The ratios 280/34, 375/39 and 62.5/18 are not mutually consistent, so they are probably not one proportional series.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a flyleaf of personal memoranda: firewood deliveries, coin dimensions and weights, and a citation of Mädler's telescope. It contains no mathematical content beyond trivial division. Gauss's interest in coin metrology and household accounts is well documented.

checkable.asserts: Klafter received from 17 to 26 May 1820 (3rd, 4th, 5th, and half of 6th) total 3.5

transcription_corrections: '4 Zoll 43 Linien' should read '4½füss[ig] 43 Linien': 4½-foot refractor, 43 lines aperture.
The A.N. number is written over; the base reading '192' is at least as likely as '162'.
'9 Doppelthaler = 369 mm 5 Breite' means 369.5 mm breadth (the superscript 'mm' sits between 369 and 5).
The upside-down 'Breite[?] 5,314' first word is uncertain; it may be a coin name ('Albus'?) rather than 'Breite'.
'leicht 58.6 / Seidn. neu schw. 63.8 / Gr.M. 64.87': 'Gr.M.' may be 'Gr.B.M.', parallel to 'Gr.BM' in the other upside-down block.
